create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl (string) as alternative.

saml.description: Token exchange may return a scope different from the requested scope because ZITADEL validates and narrows it.

conditions.scope: returned scope differs from requested scope

saml.note: Do not flag a reduced returned scope as privilege escalation or inconsistency.

saml.description: Introspection only reports active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: An inactive introspection result can be caused by the caller not being in audience, not by token invalidity.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, the returned token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: Using that field as a Bearer token will fail by design.

saml.description: When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows RFC 8693 behavior as documented by ZITADEL.

saml.description: SAML SSO endpoint errors are conveyed inside the SAML response StatusCode while the HTTP status remains 200.
saml.note: Do not treat HTTP 200 from SAML SSO as successful authentication without inspecting the protocol-level result.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows.
saml.note: IdP-initiated SAML attempts failing are expected and should not be flagged as flow breakage.

saml.description: Access tokens may be opaque rather than JWTs by default.
saml.note: Tests must not assume access_token is parseable JWT; use userinfo or introspection for verification.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint can return HTTP 200 even when authentication failed; failure is encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message inside the SAML response.
saml.note: Avoid flagging successful HTTP transport as successful authentication.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports SAML only as SP-initiated flow. The fuzzer MUST start from /oauth/v2/authorize and complete the browser/OIDC flow; do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML as a broker login path because ZITADEL documents that it supports only SP-initiated SAML.

For SAML-brokered login tests, the fuzzer MUST use the OIDC front-channel and then exchange the returned code at /oauth/v2/token. ZITADEL's documented public login/session credential is the OIDC/OAuth token, not a direct SAML ACS login API in the provided docs.

For I2 expired_token and future_token style freshness tests on exchanged or brokered tokens, include a CONTROL flow using a valid authorization request and successful code exchange. Without a control, failures at /oauth/v2/token or /oidc/v1/userinfo cannot be distinguished from broken client/app configuration.

The /oauth/v2/authorize redirect_uri must exactly match a preregistered redirect URI. Any mismatch causes invalid_grant/authorization failure and can look like a security rejection unrelated to the invariant under test.

When testing organization-scoped SAML broker behavior, the fuzzer MUST request the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} if organization-specific login policy or IdP configuration is being exercised. Otherwise ZITADEL may use default settings and the test will target the wrong IdP/policy set.

Token exchange audience narrowing is enforced: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 audience-binding tests, do not expect arbitrary new audiences to succeed; only flag success when ZITADEL accepts an audience not already present upstream.

Token exchange scope can differ from the input request because ZITADEL validates and may reduce it. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the returned scope and claims, not just HTTP 200. A successful response with narrowed scope is by design, not a violation.

Token exchange requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that access_token value as a bearer session token for subsequent API calls; use only responses with bearer-capable access_token as session_token.

ZITADEL does not support refresh_token as subject_token or actor_token in token exchange. Tests that submit refresh tokens to RFC 8693 should expect rejection and must not classify that as a security issue.
ZITADEL does not support the resource parameter in token exchange; supplying it results in invalid_target. Do not use resource-based token exchange failures as evidence of authorization binding bugs.

For token introspection, active=true also requires that the introspecting client is part of the token audience. An active=false result can therefore mean audience mismatch of the caller rather than token invalidity; the fuzzer must authenticate introspection as a client in the token audience.

JWT client assertions used for token or introspection endpoints must include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat not older than 1 hour. Failures outside that window are setup errors, not freshness or proof-integrity findings against brokered SAML login.

For I5 token-exchange wrong-audience tests, use a subject token whose audience is known and request a different audience at /oauth/v2/token. Only acceptance of a non-subset audience is suspicious; rejection is documented behavior.

For I4 cross-protocol or SAML identity merge tests, user creation through external IdPs may require mapped required fields via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. If those fields are absent, login/user creation can fail for provisioning reasons unrelated to identity binding.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML login against ZITADEL as broker/SP behavior; a valid SAML test must begin with the SP/OIDC authorization flow and then complete the brokered login.

For SAML-brokered login tests, the executable login path is OIDC-based after federation: start at /oauth/v2/authorize, complete the external SAML authentication in the browser, then exchange the returned code at /oauth/v2/token. Do NOT expect a direct documented ACS POST endpoint for forged SAMLResponse submission in the provided docs.

When testing organization-scoped SAML IdPs, the authorization request SHOULD include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may apply default instance settings instead of the organization-specific external IdP configuration, causing false positives or wrong-provider routing.

The reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces exact organization membership for the selected organization. For multi-identity I4 tests across different organizations, vary or omit this scope intentionally; do not assume wildcard or pattern matching semantics.
Token exchange resource is currently not supported. Supplying the resource parameter will always result in invalid_target. Do NOT interpret this as an authorization-binding failure.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer API credential; use requested_token_type access_token or jwt for session-bearing follow-up calls.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, ZITADEL documents that invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. A valid I5 test must compare requested scope against the original subject/actor token scope and distinguish expected narrowing/rejection from escalation.

For token exchange audience tests, when audience is omitted it is inherited from subject_token, or from actor_token if subject_token carries no audience. A valid control must account for this inheritance; otherwise an apparently broad audience may be inherited by design.

For token exchange scope tests, when scope is omitted it is inherited from subject_token, or from actor_token if subject_token carries no scope. A valid control must explicitly set scope when testing narrowing or expansion semantics.

ID tokens used as subject_token or actor_token in token exchange are currently rejected if expired. For I2 freshness tests using token exchange, include a control with a valid unexpired ID token; expired-token rejection is expected by design.

JWT Profile assertions used at /oauth/v2/token must include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, exp, iat, iss, sub, and a kid header identifying the uploaded key. iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. For I2 tests, use claims like iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls, and vary only the target freshness field under test.

The token endpoint accepts multiple grant types on the same path. The fuzzer MUST send application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies and the correct grant_type for each scenario; malformed or mixed grant parameters produce invalid_request/unsupported_grant_type and are not security findings.

The introspection endpoint reports active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification, use a client/application in the token audience; otherwise active=false is expected and must not be treated as token invalidation or audience confusion.

ZITADEL commonly issues opaque access tokens by default. For verification and authorization tests, prefer /oidc/v1/userinfo or /oauth/v2/introspect rather than assuming local JWT parsing will work. A non-JWT access token is by design, not proof of missing claims.

The authorization endpoint supports response_mode values query, fragment, and form_post, and ignores invalid values. For flow-coherence tests, do not treat fallback from an invalid response_mode as a bug; use explicit valid response_mode values in controls.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate login via /saml/v2/SSO or an OIDC authorization flow that redirects into the external SAML IdP path; IdP-initiated SAML assertions are not a valid control path for this platform.

For SAML login tests against ZITADEL as broker/SP, HTTP status alone is not authoritative. The SAML SSO endpoint documents HTTP 200 even on authentication errors, with failure encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST inspect the returned SAMLResponse content, not just HTTP status, to determine success vs failure.

For SAML signature-validation tests (saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), the fuzzer MUST configure a SAML identity provider in ZITADEL first. The public docs here expose only standard SAML/OIDC endpoints, not the provider-management REST paths; without a configured upstream SAML IdP trust relationship, login failures are not evidence of correct signature validation.

For SAML broker user-creation tests, Login V2 requires required user fields to be populated from upstream SAML attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. If this mapping is absent, first-time federated user creation can fail for missing required fields. The fuzzer MUST treat such failures as setup failures, not security rejections.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, ZITADEL may create or link users using mapped upstream attributes such as email/username when external IdP account creation/linking is enabled. The fuzzer MUST control whether automatic creation/linking and manual linking are enabled in provider settings; otherwise identity merges may be by configuration intent rather than a principal-binding flaw.

For organization-scoped SAML/OIDC login tests, if an organization overrides default login settings or IdPs, the authorization request MUST include scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}. Without this scope, ZITADEL uses default settings and the test may hit the wrong IdP or policy, causing false positives/negatives.

Token exchange audience is restrictive by design: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain subject/actor tokens whose audiences are known, then request an audience outside that set as the attack. Rejection is expected behavior, not a bug.

Token exchange scope can legitimately differ from the original request because ZITADEL allows changing scope and then validates the final scope. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation, the fuzzer MUST compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope/claims against upstream authorization and requested scope, not assume any scope change is a vulnerability.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness controls around token exchange, the fuzzer MUST include a valid-token control alongside expired/future-token attacks to distinguish intended expiry enforcement from broken setup.

The token introspection endpoint only returns active=true if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST introspect with a client/application that is in the token audience; otherwise active=false is expected and must not be misread as token invalidity or revocation.

JWT-based client authentication to token/introspection endpoints requires aud to include ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls. Failures outside this window are expected setup failures.

Reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces organization membership. For multi-tenant authorization tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this scope narrowing behavior; login failure with a non-member user is expected and not an authorization-binding bug.
The resource parameter in token exchange is currently not supported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource for audience-binding tests on ZITADEL; use audience instead.

ZITADEL supports both opaque and JWT access tokens. For verification steps, the fuzzer MUST use /oidc/v1/userinfo with a user access token or /oauth/v2/introspect with proper client auth, rather than assuming local JWT parsing is sufficient or always possible.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
